title: a refused loopback dial wakes the database proxy through the bus
intention: When the db client's TCP loopback dial (no Postgres socket on the box) is refused, the client asks the bus once to start the database proxy and retries the dial for up to 60 s; any other failure, or a wake that fails, raises at once naming why (outline 11.3.9).
why: Measured 2026-11-18 on akiendelllinux at 44d22f516: store.py connect() and ensure_database() call psycopg2.connect once with no retry (store.py:123 and :141), so on a cache box where the database proxy is not running (after a reboot, nothing starts it) every db call fails 'Connection refused' at 127.0.0.1:5432. dbproxy's charter files this edge as 'the db client waking the proxy on a refused connection (db_domain's own ticket)'. The bus opens its own table lazily (bus.py:333, boot-order law), so a bus can start and carry 'database start' while the database is refused.
traces_to: Outline 11.3.9 and 11.3.7 (every box's processes reach the database through its own proxy); outline 5.8.3.2.1 (the device is woken when it is needed); Law 7 (a failed wake is loud).
how: store.py gains _dial(dbname): psycopg2.connect over _conn_args(); on an OperationalError whose text says the connection was refused, and only when the dial is TCP (no 'host' socket dir), it calls _wake_proxy() once per process and retries every 0.5 s until _WAKE_SECONDS (60) pass. _wake_proxy imports cairn.tools.bus_client.remote at call time and runs ensure_bus() then RemoteBus().verbs('cairn.devices.dbproxy.shim:DatabaseProxyShim', ['start']), a string target, so store.py imports no cairn.devices.dbproxy. A wake that raises, or answers a non-zero exit, re-raises the refusal with the wake's failure attached. ensure_database() and connect() dial through _dial.

clauses.claim: a refused TCP loopback dial wakes the proxy exactly once and the dial is retried until it connects
a socket dial that fails, and a TCP failure that is not a refusal, raise at once and never wake
a wake that fails, or a refusal still standing after the retry window, raises the refusal naming why
the wake asks the bus for start on cairn.devices.dbproxy.shim:DatabaseProxyShim, a class that exists, and store.py imports nothing from cairn.devices.dbproxy

decisions.text: D1: store.py: _dial, _refused, _wake_proxy and _WAKE_SECONDS; connect() and ensure_database() dial through _dial; the bus client is imported inside _wake_proxy, at call time.

D2: the proof monkeypatches psycopg2.connect, the wake and the bus client in-process, one tooth per clause, shaped like cairn/devices/db_domain/tools/client/proofs/test_the_passfile_survives_a_repointed_instance_root.py.

measured.saw: store.py dials psycopg2.connect once with no retry at :123 and :141; dbproxy's charter files the wake edge to db_domain; bus.py _ensure is lazy
measured.how: read store.py, cairn/devices/dbproxy/intention+why.json filed_edges and bus.py:333 on akiendelllinux at 44d22f516
